Abstract:

As organizations increasingly rely on innovation to remain competitive, understanding how to&nbspcultivate innovative work behavior (IWB) among employees has become a strategic priority.&nbspThis study, rooted in the Job Demands&ndashResources (JD-R) framework, examines the roles of&nbspproactive personality, inclusive leadership, and climate for innovation as critical antecedents&nbspthat foster employee engagement (EE) among millennial professionals in the Indian&nbspinformation technology (IT) sector. It further investigates how EE contributes to IWB directly&nbspand indirectly via constructive deviant behavior (CDB), a form of intentional deviation from&nbsporganizational norms aimed at generating positive outcomes. Additionally, the study explores
how challenge and hindrance stressors differentially moderate the relationship between EE&nbspand CDB, as well as the overall indirect pathway from EE to IWB through CDB. Data were&nbspcollected through a structured questionnaire administered to millennial IT employees across&nbspIndia and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM).&nbspFindings reveal that EE significantly mediates the influence of proactive personality, inclusive&nbspleadership, and climate for innovation on IWB. CDB acts as a positive behavioral conduit&nbsptranslating engagement into innovation, particularly under conditions of high challenge&nbspstressors and low hindrance stressors. The moderated mediation results underscore the critical
role of job demands in shaping the engagement-to-innovation pathway. Theoretically, this&nbspstudy extends the JD-R model by integrating CDB as a mediating mechanism and incorporating&nbspstressor types as boundary conditions. It advances the literature on positive deviance and&nbspinnovation by elucidating how personal and contextual resources interact with work stressors&nbspto drive innovative outcomes. Practically, the findings offer actionable insights for HR&nbspprofessionals and organizational leaders. Interventions should focus on fostering inclusive and&nbspinnovation-supportive climates, promoting proactive behavior, and managing stressor types to&nbspoptimize engagement and innovation. The study is particularly relevant to organizations
seeking to harness the creative potential of millennial employees in dynamic and high-pressure&nbspenvironments.
